dispositions.claim: An authenticated client sharing the configured API-key principal can derive another session's capability from a known or guessable prompt_cache_key; this is an inference from the deterministic derivation and digest-only authorization
dispositions.evidence: src/serve/client_identity.cpp:65-70,85-100 hashes the raw cache key without a secret and installs it as client_session_sha256; src/serve/http_server.cpp:562-587,614-623 accepts that digest alone for checkpoint deletion after API-key authentication
dispositions.verification: council-verification.md finding 7: client_identity.cpp:65-70,85-100; http_server.cpp:384-405,561-587,614-623; ResourceManager private/principal scope comparisons; docs/serving.md:986-1009.
dispositions.change: Record product limitation: Within one API-key principal, prompt_cache_key names a session capability; use unique high-entropy keys and do not share that principal among mutually untrusted clients.
dispositions.rationale: Knowing the same cache key selects the same documented capability; no distinct-digest bypass was found. Mutually hostile users sharing one bearer principal are outside the declared single-trusted-user boundary. No authentication redesign or blocking in-scope P1 remains.

dispositions.claim: Quota enforcement can destroy an inactive unrelated session's current checkpoint before the requesting session's save commits, so a later stale-publication or I/O refusal cannot preserve all prior durable authority
dispositions.evidence: src/serve/session_checkpoint_store.cpp:1175-1183,1261-1292 includes other sessions' current directories as reclaim candidates and tombstones/deletes them; src/serve/session_checkpoint_store.cpp:2045-2087 executes that sweep before publish_export and can subsequently return a refusal

dispositions.change: F2: plan current victims before publication; delete current-session victims only after acknowledged new-current publication, with at most one quota-bounded incoming set of transient physical space; stuck cleanup cannot accumulate another over-quota transient.
dispositions.rationale: The prior requester-only guard did not protect inactive unrelated current generations. Executed red-at-F quota assertions and green corrected union establish preservation on stale/refused publication without an unbounded quota exemption.

dispositions.claim: The current pointer is unauthenticated, so an on-disk writer can replay an older authentic generation even under strict origin: the MAC binds a generation's content, not which generation is published

dispositions.change: none; retain this explicit freshness limitation for v0.13.1 assessment.
dispositions.rationale: An actor able to replace checkpoint files can replay authentic old state. Adding an external rollback-resistant counter would introduce persistent authority beyond this localized remediation; strict mode protects forgery, not replay of authentic generations.

residual_risks: Within one API-key principal, prompt_cache_key names a session capability; use unique high-entropy keys and do not share that principal among mutually untrusted clients. No distinct-digest scope bypass was found.

Windows K6 code at F is not a qualified shipping path for v0.13.0 RTX 5090. Main reports the native-line correction; Windows execution and native release acceptance remain v0.13.1 gates, not Linux-proof claims.
Runtime-image base selection is digest-pinned but not automatically cross-checked against the selected source runtime-base receipt; workflow binding enhancement is deferred to v0.13.1.

Superseded durable-owner metadata can retain reclamation-ineligible owners. F2 preserves committed owners across abandonment but does not demonstrate superseded-tag clearing; defer that distinct capacity issue to v0.13.1.
Authenticated session churn can grow Engine gate metadata over process lifetime. There is no demonstrated map-size bound or pruning fix; lifecycle-safe retirement is deferred to v0.13.1.

Native import and victim validation retain finite payload I/O/hash work on the device worker and may stall decode. This residual latency is distinct from the removed Responses-mutex deadlock; reassess in v0.13.1.
Legacy rollback roots must remain separate from the new runtime root. No claim is made that quota garbage collection preserves an unsupported legacy root selected by an operator.
MAC authentication proves origin/content, not monotonic freshness: a filesystem writer can replay an older authentic generation. Anti-replay authority is not introduced in this localized remediation.
Failed/stale publication may leave bounded orphan-generation work until cleanup; targeted efficiency changes are deferred rather than claimed fixed by the quota-atomicity repair.
Model/binary identity is measured by the supported managed lifecycle. Manually bypassed launches that assert incorrect hashes are not certified by this release ledger.
Exact-profile F2 uses strict origin authentication; generic non-strict CLI compatibility remains available outside that product profile and must not be used to import untrusted checkpoint material.
